records.label: Long COVID diagnosis after acute infection

grade.label: Source discrepancies retained
grade.rationale: The correction-access task is complete: COVID-OUT’s actual notice and corrected table were checked. Its Discussion and current registry still disagree with that table, and selective follow-up limits inference. ACTIV-6 contributes an uncertain secondary diagnosis effect and a negative primary symptom decision. No settled benefit letter is assigned to this conservatively held synthesis.

effect.label: Uncertain reduction
effect.detail: HR 0.59 in corrected COVID-OUT report; -0.7 percentage points in ACTIV-6
effect.rationale: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID in its corrected report. ACTIV-6’s secondary diagnosis estimate favored metformin, but its absolute interval included no difference and its primary symptom result did not meet the efficacy threshold. Estimates remain separate; no clinical-importance threshold or pooled effect is imposed.

records.label: Sustained recovery with higher-dose fluvoxamine

grade.label: Benefit not demonstrated
grade.rationale: The masked randomized comparison directly informs this symptom-recovery endpoint, and the credible interval is close to no effect. Postrandomization drug-delivery exclusions, participant-reported recovery, a skeptical Bayesian prior and the selected Omicron-era population leave uncertainty about smaller effects and applicability; the result is informative without proving equivalence. The benefit letter addresses this endpoint only, separately from confidence in the selected-source finding.

effect.label: HR 0.99
effect.detail: 95% credible interval 0.89–1.09; median recovery 10 days in each group

The modified intention-to-treat analysis included 1175 of 1208 randomized participants; 33 without timely drug delivery were excluded after randomization. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

records.label: Visceral adiposity during healthy aging

grade.label: Benefit not demonstrated
grade.rationale: The masked randomized design directly addresses visceral adiposity at 48 weeks, but the small completer-only sample, missing DXA observations, broad intervals and reduced bioavailability of the compounded preparation leave substantial uncertainty. No primary VAT benefit was demonstrated; this surrogate finding cannot establish lifespan extension or rule out an adiposity effect. The benefit letter addresses this endpoint only, separately from confidence in the selected-source finding.

effect.label: No clear VAT difference
effect.detail: Improvement OR 1.81 at 5 mg; 1.68 at 10 mg, both with wide intervals
effect.rationale: PEARL did not demonstrate a difference in its primary visceral-adiposity outcome. Dose-specific odds ratios for improvement were 1.81 (95% CI 0.73–4.50) at 5 mg and 1.68 (0.66–4.32) at 10 mg; both intervals included no difference. This was a small completer analysis: 125 randomized, 114 completed (40 at 5 mg, 35 at 10 mg, 39 placebo); missing outcome values were removed pairwise. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

records.label: Lean tissue in women during healthy aging

grade.label: Possible benefit
grade.rationale: The reported between-group lean-tissue contrast favors 10 mg compounded rapamycin in women, but few women contributed, endpoint-specific observations were missing, and this was a secondary subgroup among many analyses. Confidence in a general clinical benefit is low despite the positive adjusted comparison; muscle function, sarcopenia treatment and longevity were not demonstrated. The benefit letter addresses this endpoint only, separately from confidence in the selected-source finding.

effect.label: +6.194 percentage points
effect.rationale: Women in the 10 mg group had a larger percentage change in lean tissue mass than placebo: between-group difference 6.194 percentage points (95% CI 0.8773–11.5105; Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.018). This small secondary subgroup finding does not demonstrate longer life or better physical function. The positive finding is a small secondary sex-specific comparison amid many body-composition and survey analyses; replication and clinical importance remain uncertain. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

records.label: Periodontal bone in aged mice

grade.label: Nonclinical evidence only
grade.rationale: Two controlled mouse cohorts and repeated imaging support an experimental bone finding, but small female-only groups, model-specific exposures and incomplete reporting of allocation concealment prevent a confident human clinical inference. The evidence is explicitly preclinical, with no human trial count, treatment effect or benefit letter. These experiments cannot establish clinical benefit, so no A–F benefit letter is assigned.

effect.label: Animal finding
effect.detail: More periodontal bone after 8 weeks; clinical magnitude unknown
effect.rationale: Rapamycin-treated aged mice had more periodontal bone than vehicle controls; longitudinal scans in one colony also showed bone gain relative to baseline. This is an animal finding and does not establish periodontal benefit in people. Only female mice were studied, with small colony-specific groups; human dose, durability and clinical benefit were not established. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

records.label: Growth of WNT-TCF-dependent colorectal xenografts

grade.label: Nonclinical evidence only
grade.rationale: The report links xenograft growth inhibition to TCF dependence using negative and rescue controls, but the findings arise from cell and immunodeficient-mouse models at nonclinical exposures. Small experiments, no human comparator and unresolved translation leave weak support for any clinical colorectal-cancer inference; no A–F clinical benefit grade is assigned. These experiments cannot establish clinical benefit, so no A–F benefit letter is assigned.

effect.label: Cell/mouse finding
effect.detail: TCF-dependent growth inhibition; negative and rescue controls retained
effect.rationale: Ivermectin inhibited growth of WNT-TCF-dependent colorectal xenografts; TCF-independent growth was not similarly inhibited, and constitutively active TCF rescued growth. These experiments support a pathway hypothesis rather than clinical colorectal-cancer efficacy. Preclinical model, nonclinical route and exposure, small experimental groups and incomplete allocation/blinding information prevent a clinical efficacy inference. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.

effect.detail: Reduced A549 xenograft growth over 12 days; clinical benefit untested
effect.rationale: Fenbendazole reduced A549 xenograft size and weight in the reported mouse experiment, with supporting apoptosis and vascularity assays. Randomization, allocation concealment and blinded tumor assessment were not established; a numeric effect and confidence interval were not extracted. No clinical-importance magnitude category has been assigned.
